name: GA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+36 partisan lean makes a Democratic win the overwhelming default
Incumbent Nikema Williams is renominated and seeking another term
Republican challenger shows no measurable fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side at 99%
model.rationale: This Atlanta-based seat carries a D+36 partisan lean, and incumbent Nikema Williams is renominated with a substantial fundraising edge over a challenger who reports no money on hand. Prediction markets price the Democratic side at 99%, and no polls or expert ratings suggest any competitive threat, so the forecast sits firmly in Safe D territory with a margin in the low thirties.
model.watch: A surprise could only come from an unforeseen scandal or a third-party disruption, since no polling, fundraising, or rating evidence points to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 5th District, anchored in Atlanta, is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+36. Incumbent Nikema Williams is running for another term after easily securing her party's nomination, and she has raised roughly $600,000 for the cycle.

Her Republican opponent, John Oscar Salvesen, reports no fundraising or outside spending, and no public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances at 99%. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the only real question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
